We've now worked through all the main flows *and* the tricky edge situations, and your recent reactions have been consistent approvals. I think we've fully explored the scope for this first version. Here's everything that's settled — this is what I'd build:

**Saving & titles**
- Paste a link, optionally add tags, save. It appears instantly, and the page's real title fills in on its own. If a title can't be read, the address stands in until you rename it.

**Organizing**
- Links carry multiple tags (not single folders). As you type a tag, your existing tags are suggested (most-used first) so you don't create near-duplicates.
- Edit a bookmark's title and tags together via the pencil, reviewing before you save.

**Finding**
- Browse by tag from the top row or from a link's own tags.
- Search across titles, addresses, and tags at once, with matches highlighted; search narrows within the tag you're browsing, and a friendly message shows when nothing matches.

**Read-later queue**
- Opt links into a "To read" queue, see only those, and "Mark read" to clear them from the queue (the bookmark stays).

**Archiving & deleting**
- Archive to tuck a link out of your normal view (and out of search/queue), with a separate Archived tab to find and restore it — one click, reversible.
- Delete permanently from inside the edit form, with a confirmation that names the link and points you to Archive as the safe alternative.

**Dependability & clean input**
- Everything persists across sessions — links, tags, read status, archive status.
- Invalid addresses are blocked with a hint; duplicates aren't re-added — you're pointed to the existing one (even if archived).
- It's your personal collection on your own device — no accounts or login in this version.

**Noted for later (not in this version):** saving a full copy of each page, per-link notes/descriptions, and an undo/trash for deletion.

That's **10 settled behaviors**. **May I now start building this as the real application?** Once you approve, I'll switch from exploring to actually implementing it.
